<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged experiment and determine whether it is healthy. Inspect the
source, launch script, metrics, rollouts and debug evidence. If you find a
defect, repair it in `/workspace`. Do not launch training; the system performs
the graded rerun after your response. Cheap non-training checks are allowed.

**Do not use the network.** Do not fetch code, documentation, packages,
or any other material from outside the staged workspace — diagnose and
repair using only what is staged locally.

Write `/workspace/report.md` describing the root cause, every changed file and
the expected metric effect. A missing report scores zero.

The system deletes `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then runs:

```bash
bash run_experiment.sh
```

The fixed experiment must preserve the supplied Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8
bundle, deterministic GSM8K 16/8 subset, rollout n=4, response length 32,
temperature 0.8, KL coefficient 0.05, four GRPO updates, seed and one-GPU
layout. Do not alter rewards, data, model, budget or metric logging. The grader
reads only fresh files under `experiment_logs`: the final-step
validation health metrics, cross-checked against verl's own per-step file
log (including the per-update KL loss) and the rollout sync probe the run
writes, with the launch script and the health instrumentation pinned by
sha256. Copying or fabricating metrics scores zero.
I’ll inspect the staged code, launch script, metrics, rollouts, and debug evidence, then repair any defect and write `/workspace/report.md`. I won’t launch training or use the network.

steps.message: I found two PiSSA-specific defects. Reference scoring disables the adapter, which exposes the residual weights rather than the original policy. Rollout sync loads the original model first, then adds the full PiSSA adapter, double-counting its initial contribution. I’ll use the frozen initial adapter for reference scoring and export the current merged actor weights on every rollout sync.

+        self.batch = tensors or {}
+        self.meta_info = meta_info or {}
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_dict(cls, tensors, meta_info=None):
+        return cls(tensors, meta_info)
+
+
+class ReferenceHarness:
+    """Only the model forward and adapter API are supplied by this harness."""
+
+    _is_lora = True
+    _is_svd_init = True
+
+    def __init__(self, model):
+        self.model = model
+
+    @contextlib.contextmanager
+    def _svd_init_adapter_ctx(self):
+        previous = self.model.active_adapters[0]
+        self.model.set_adapter("_base_ref")
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            self.model.set_adapter(previous)
+
+    def compute_log_prob(self, data):
+        disable = data.meta_info.pop("is_lora", False)
+        with self.model.disable_adapter() if disable else contextlib.nullcontext(), torch.no_grad():
+            log_probs = torch.log_softmax(self.model(data.batch["inputs"]) / 0.8, dim=-1)
+        return Batch.from_dict({"old_log_probs": log_probs})
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("output_key", ["ref_log_prob", "base_ref_log_prob"])
+def test_reference_stays_at_initial_policy_when_actor_changes(model, output_key):
+    compute_reference = load_function(
+        "workers/fsdp_workers.py", "_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor", {"DataProto": Batch}
+    )
+    worker = ReferenceHarness(model)
+    data = Batch({"inputs": torch.eye(4)})
+    initial = worker.compute_log_prob(data).batch["old_log_probs"].clone()
+    actual = compute_reference(worker, data, output_key).batch[output_key]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, initial, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    # Perturb a toy adapter directly; no optimizer or training is run.
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        model.base_model.model.proj.lora_B["default"].weight.add_(0.3)
+    changed = worker.compute_log_prob(data).batch["old_log_probs"]
+    assert not torch.allclose(changed, initial)
+    actual = compute_reference(worker, data, output_key).batch[output_key]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, initial, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert model.active_adapters == ["default"]
+    worker._is_svd_init = False
+    actual = compute_reference(worker, data, output_key).batch[output_key]
+    with model.disable_adapter(), torch.no_grad():
+        residual = torch.log_softmax(model(data.batch["inputs"]) / 0.8, dim=-1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, residual, rtol=0, atol=0)

+class Config(dict):
+    __getattr__ = dict.__getitem__

+class CapturingRollout:
+    sleep_level = 2
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.calls = []
+
+    async def resume(self, tags):
+        pass
+
+    async def update_weights(self, weights, **kwargs):
+        self.calls.append((dict(weights), kwargs))
+
+
+def test_every_sync_exports_current_policy_without_adapter_delta(model, collect_merged):
+    def no_op(*args, **kwargs):
+        pass
+
+    def unexpected_lora_delta(**kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("Residual-base policies must not enter the ordinary LoRA delta path")
+
+    namespace = {
+        "aggressive_empty_cache": no_op,
+        "log_gpu_memory_usage": no_op,
+        "logger": logging.getLogger(__name__),
+        "collect_merged_peft_params": collect_merged,
+        "collect_lora_params": unexpected_lora_delta,
+        "convert_weight_keys": lambda weights, _: weights,
+        "set_expandable_segments": no_op,
+        "get_device_id": lambda: "cpu",
+        "get_torch_device": lambda: torch,
+        "DTensor": type("UnusedDTensor", (), {}),
+        "check_exclude_modules": lambda config, key: False,

+    rollout_mode = load_function("workers/fsdp_workers.py", "rollout_mode", namespace)
+    worker = SimpleNamespace(
+        actor_module_fsdp=model,
+        _is_offload_param=False,
+        _is_svd_init=True,
+        base_sync_done=False,
+        rank=1,  # Do not write debug/metric artifacts from this unit test.

*** Add File: /workspace/report.md
+# Staged experiment repair
+
+The recorded experiment is unhealthy. Two code paths treat a PiSSA residual-base bundle as ordinary LoRA, producing an incorrect KL reference and an inconsistent rollout policy. The repair changes policy handling, not the experiment settings or measurements.
+
+## Evidence and root cause
+
+The supplied rank-8 bundle represents the policy as `W_res + s B_t A_t`, where `W_res = W_0 - s B_0 A_0` and `s = alpha/r = 1`. Its frozen initial policy is therefore `W_res + s B_0 A_0`. Disabling the adapter exposes only `W_res`.
+
+1. **Wrong reference for both the training KL loss and base-model KL diagnostics.** In `ActorRolloutRefWorker._compute_base_log_prob_from_actor`, the SVD-init branch set `is_lora=True`, causing `compute_log_prob` to disable adapters. Although initialization correctly loaded a frozen `_base_ref` adapter, this branch never used it. Both `compute_ref_log_prob` and `compute_base_ref_log_prob` consequently evaluated the residual model. In `observed_run/metrics/all_steps.jsonl`, the four `actor/kl_loss` values are 0.761803, 0.929668, 0.975083, and 0.879964. The first pre-update base-model diagnostic is -4.075873, even before the initial actor should differ from its reference. The first three updates have zero policy-gradient loss but nonzero gradient norms, consistent with the incorrect KL penalty driving updates. The base-model diagnostic is a signed sampled log-probability difference; its negative sign alone is not the defect.
+
+2. **Wrong rollout synchronization for a residual-base adapter.** The initial sync loaded the original pretrained checkpoint instead of exporting the actor; later syncs entered the ordinary LoRA delta branch. With a retained original base, adding the full current PiSSA adapter yields `W_0 + s B_t A_t`, double-counting the initial low-rank contribution relative to the actor. The separate sleep-level-2 base reload can also make this behavior depend on the rollout lifecycle. The staged probes explicitly record `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` initially and `lora_delta` subsequently. A rollout should instead evaluate the current actor `W_res + s B_t A_t` consistently on every sync.
+
+3. **Merged-export storage aliasing.** The existing merged-weight collector used `detach().cpu()`. For CPU parameters that operation shares storage; its subsequent `unmerge_adapter()` silently changes the exported weights back to residual weights. A tiny PEFT forward-only reproduction measured a maximum export/output discrepancy of 0.265121 before the fix. Export tensors now own their storage.
+
+The rollout and validation evidence supports investigating policy correctness rather than tuning rewards: training outputs often omit the required answer marker, the final validation outputs are all incorrect, and validation accuracy finishes at 0/8. Some training outputs receive legitimate nonzero reward at update 4; completion and nonzero gradients/rewards do not establish policy health. The supplied historical metric file has no `val-health/*` entries, so no historical final-health value is claimed here.
+
+Local checkpoint inspection also confirms the residual interpretation: in the first q-projection, mean absolute residual-versus-original weight difference is 0.0298342, while adding the saved adapter reduces reconstruction error to 0.0000806333. The small remaining error is consistent with the supplied bfloat16 bundle. The staged adapter contains 96 tensors with rank 8, and the parquet subsets contain exactly 16 training and 8 validation rows.
+
+## Every changed file
+
+- `verl/verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py`: the SVD reference branch evaluates the frozen initial adapter through the existing context manager, with adapters enabled. This repairs both reference callers. Every SVD rollout sync now collects the current merged actor, maps names to the existing vLLM base-layer wrappers, and sends full weights with no PEFT adapter configuration. The obsolete original-checkpoint rollout loader was removed. The existing sync probe truthfully reports `merged_full_weights` for this path.
+- `verl/verl/utils/fsdp_utils.py`: merged exports make independent CPU tensor copies before unmerging, preserving the exported policy even when actor parameters already reside on CPU.
+- `verl/tests/workers/test_pissa_policy_sync_cpu.py`: four focused CPU regressions exercise the actual source functions with tiny PEFT layers. They check merged-export values and storage independence, both reference output keys before and after a manual toy-adapter perturbation, ordinary-LoRA reference behavior, and three successive full-weight syncs with no additional adapter. No optimizer, training loop, checkpoint update, or experiment metrics are involved.
+- `report.md`: this diagnosis, change inventory, checks, and expected effects.
+
+## Expected fresh metric effects
+
+- `val-health/base_reference_mae` should fall to approximately zero and `val-health/base_reference_consistency` should approach 1: the production reference now evaluates the frozen initial policy used by the unchanged independent health oracle.
+- `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae` should decrease and `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement` should increase toward 1 because actor and rollout now use the same effective weights. Backend precision and log-probability conventions can leave a residual difference.
+- The genuine per-update `actor/kl_loss` should be much smaller than the recorded 0.76–0.98, especially at initialization. Later values should reflect real actor drift from the frozen reference, rather than removal of the PiSSA initialization. KL coefficient 0.05 and its existing loss/logging implementation remain intact. The initial signed base-model KL diagnostic should also be close to zero.
+- The initial and latest rollout sync probes should both report `merged_full_weights`, `rollout_has_peft_config=false`, and `is_svd_init=true`. Full-weight transfers on each sync cost more than adapter-only transfers but do not change the four-update budget or GPU layout.
+- Validation accuracy and rewards may change when the correct policy is sampled. Improvement on eight validation examples is not guaranteed and has not been measured here.
+
+## Checks and preserved constraints
+
+Passed: four CPU regression tests in 3.33 seconds, Python syntax checks for all changed Python files, and `bash -n run_experiment.sh`. Ruff passed on the utility and tests, and on the worker with its three pre-existing long-line findings excluded; those unchanged lines include instrumentation and were left intact. The new test file passes the formatter check.
+
+The CPU tests load selected source functions without importing the full worker stack. A normal worker import in this inspection environment fails because its installed TensorDict lacks `LinkedList`; its Torch/PEFT/Transformers versions also differ from the recorded training image. No dependencies were fetched or altered. Ray, CUDA, and vLLM integration remain for the system's graded rerun.
+
+SHA256 checks confirm that the launch script, trainer health instrumentation, actor loss/metric implementation, file logger, rollout server instrumentation, independent expected-reference function, adapter context manager, and debug writer helpers are unchanged. In particular, `run_experiment.sh` remains `cbf2b661de29a53f1d6aaa752cc9eef2389508a55782c673b9c54342fa99658b`, and `verl/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py` remains `4e2231b24b4b5b0381a012ea348d2f51e1666ec4f4a4cdd55953a20335d1d6f8`.
+
+The supplied Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8 assets, data, rewards, seed settings, rollout n=4, response length 32, temperature 0.8, KL coefficient 0.05, four GRPO updates, and one-GPU layout are preserved. No training was launched, no network was used, and no files were created or modified under `experiment_logs`. All reported training numbers above are explicitly historical evidence; the system must generate fresh metrics for the repaired experiment.
*** End Patch"));

The first three updates have zero policy-gradient loss but nonzero gradient norms, consistent with the incorrect KL penalty driving updates. The base-model diagnostic is a signed sampled log-probability difference; its negative sign alone is not the defect.
+
+2. **Wrong rollout synchronization for a residual-base adapter.** The initial sync loaded the original pretrained checkpoint instead of exporting the actor; later syncs entered the ordinary LoRA delta branch. With a retained original base, adding the full current PiSSA adapter yields `W_0 + s B_t A_t`, double-counting the initial low-rank contribution relative to the actor. The separate sleep-level-2 base reload can also make this behavior depend on the rollout lifecycle. The staged probes explicitly record `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` initially and `lora_delta` subsequently. A rollout should instead evaluate the current actor `W_res + s B_t A_t` consistently on every sync.
+
+3. **Merged-export storage aliasing.** The existing merged-weight collector used `detach().cpu()`. For CPU parameters that operation shares storage; its subsequent `unmerge_adapter()` silently changes the exported weights back to residual weights. A tiny PEFT forward-only reproduction measured a maximum export/output discrepancy of 0.265121 before the fix. Export tensors now own their storage.
+
+The rollout and validation evidence supports investigating policy correctness rather than tuning rewards: training outputs often omit the required answer marker, the final validation outputs are all incorrect, and validation accuracy finishes at 0/8. Some training outputs receive legitimate nonzero reward at update 4; completion and nonzero gradients/rewards do not establish policy health. The supplied historical metric file has no `val-health/*` entries, so no historical final-health value is claimed here.
+
+Local checkpoint inspection also confirms the residual interpretation: in the first q-projection, mean absolute residual-versus-original weight difference is 0.0298342, while adding the saved adapter reduces reconstruction error to 0.0000806333. The small remaining error is consistent with the supplied bfloat16 bundle. The staged adapter contains 96 tensors with rank 8, and the parquet subsets contain exactly 16 training and 8 validation rows.
+
+## Every changed file
+
+- `verl/verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py`: the SVD reference branch evaluates the frozen initial adapter through the existing context manager, with adapters enabled. This repairs both reference callers. Every SVD rollout sync now collects the current merged actor, maps names to the existing vLLM base-layer wrappers, and sends full weights with no PEFT adapter configuration. The obsolete original-checkpoint rollout loader was removed. The existing sync probe truthfully reports `merged_full_weights` for this path.
+- `verl/verl/utils/fsdp_utils.py`: merged exports make independent CPU tensor copies before unmerging, preserving the exported policy even when actor parameters already reside on CPU.
+- `verl/tests/workers/test_pissa_policy_sync_cpu.py`: four focused CPU regressions exercise the actual source functions with tiny PEFT layers. They check merged-export values and storage independence, both reference output keys before and after a manual toy-adapter perturbation, ordinary-LoRA reference behavior, and three successive full-weight syncs with no additional adapter. No optimizer, training loop, checkpoint update, or experiment metrics are involved.
+- `report.md`: this diagnosis, change inventory, checks, and expected effects.
+
+## Expected fresh metric effects
+
+- `val-health/base_reference_mae` should fall to approximately zero and `val-health/base_reference_consistency` should approach 1: the production reference now evaluates the frozen initial policy used by the unchanged independent health oracle.
+- `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae` should decrease and `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement` should increase toward 1 because actor and rollout now use the same effective weights. Backend precision and log-probability conventions can leave a residual difference.
+- The genuine per-update `actor/kl_loss` should be much smaller than the recorded 0.76–0.98, especially at initialization. Later values should reflect real actor drift from the frozen reference, rather than removal of the PiSSA initialization. KL coefficient 0.05 and its existing loss/logging implementation remain intact. The initial signed base-model KL diagnostic should also be close to zero.
+- The initial and latest rollout sync probes should both report `merged_full_weights`, `rollout_has_peft_config=false`, and `is_svd_init=true`. Full-weight transfers on each sync cost more than adapter-only transfers but do not change the four-update budget or GPU layout.
+- Validation accuracy and rewards may change when the correct policy is sampled. Improvement on eight validation examples is not guaranteed and has not been measured here.
+
+## Checks and preserved constraints
+
+Passed: four CPU regression tests in 3.33 seconds, Python syntax checks for all changed Python files, and `bash -n run_experiment.sh`. Ruff passed on the utility and tests, and on the worker with its three pre-existing long-line findings excluded; those unchanged lines include instrumentation and were left intact. The new test file passes the formatter check.
+
+The CPU tests load selected source functions without importing the full worker stack. A normal worker import in this inspection environment fails because its installed TensorDict lacks `LinkedList`; its Torch/PEFT/Transformers versions also differ from the recorded training image. No dependencies were fetched or altered. Ray, CUDA, and vLLM integration remain for the system's graded rerun.
+
+SHA256 checks confirm that the launch script, trainer health instrumentation, actor loss/metric implementation, file logger, rollout server instrumentation, independent expected-reference function, adapter context manager, and debug writer helpers are unchanged. In particular, `run_experiment.sh` remains `cbf2b661de29a53f1d6aaa752cc9eef2389508a55782c673b9c54342fa99658b`, and `verl/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py` remains `4e2231b24b4b5b0381a012ea348d2f51e1666ec4f4a4cdd55953a20335d1d6f8`.
+
+The supplied Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8 assets, data, rewards, seed settings, rollout n=4, response length 32, temperature 0.8, KL coefficient 0.05, four GRPO updates, and one-GPU layout are preserved. No training was launched, no network was used, and no files were created or modified under `experiment_logs`. All reported training numbers above are explicitly historical evidence; the system must generate fresh metrics for the repaired experiment.
*** End Patch"));
